future_metric_ii_c.defined_for: a given budget, to be evaluated once a causal predictor exists

formula_variables.causal_baseline_miss_bytes: miss bytes of a declared causal baseline (e.g. Global-LRU) at a given budget
formula_variables.oracle_miss_bytes: miss bytes of Oracle-Global-Belady at that same budget (the denominator's anchor: the full informational upper bound this experiment, R2-04, establishes)
formula_variables.predictor_miss_bytes: miss bytes of a future causal working-set predictor (II-C) at that same budget

future_metric_ii_c.name: fraction_of_oracle_headroom_recovered
future_metric_ii_c.purpose: the clean scientific bridge from II-A's upper bound (this experiment) to II-C's demonstrated causal recovery -- documented now so II-C has an unambiguous, predeclared metric to report against, never computed here (no predictor exists yet).
future_metric_ii_c.status: NOT_YET_SUPPORTED -- no causal predictor exists yet (II-C, R2-09..R2-12)

not_yet_supported.claim: A causal predictor will recover X% of the Oracle headroom.

not_yet_supported.claim: The Oracle gap itself is recoverable by a practical predictor.

supported_now.claim: At the tested 4 GiB budget, Oracle-Global-Belady establishes an upper-bound information headroom of 0.5859 relative miss-byte reduction over Global-LRU.

At the tested 1.5 GiB budget, the Oracle-Global-Belady comparison establishes a potentially recoverable information headroom (upper bound) of 0.4411 relative miss-byte reduction, and 103574900736 absolute miss-byte reduction, over Global-LRU.

At the tested 2 GiB budget, the Oracle-Global-Belady comparison establishes a potentially recoverable information headroom (upper bound) of 0.4755 relative miss-byte reduction, and 93423513600 absolute miss-byte reduction, over Global-LRU.

At the tested 4 GiB budget, the Oracle-Global-Belady comparison establishes a potentially recoverable information headroom (upper bound) of 0.5859 relative miss-byte reduction, and 59855155200 absolute miss-byte reduction, over Global-LRU.

At the tested 8 GiB budget, the Oracle-Global-Belady comparison establishes a potentially recoverable information headroom (upper bound) of 0.7066 relative miss-byte reduction, and 16179056640 absolute miss-byte reduction, over Global-LRU.

At the tested 16 GiB budget, the Oracle-Global-Belady comparison establishes a potentially recoverable information headroom (upper bound) of 0.0000 relative miss-byte reduction, and 0 absolute miss-byte reduction, over Global-LRU.

At the 16 GiB budget (the first tested budget exhibiting policy convergence), Global-LRU and Oracle-Global-Belady produced identical miss counts, identical miss bytes, and zero evictions each; this is the observed effective-residency point for the tested sweep, not a claim about the mathematically minimal required capacity.
The observed relative information-headroom-fraction curve across the tested budget sweep is classified as: collapse_at_effective_residency.
